title: Bridge taylorWithinEval to expPartialSum for Remainder Axiom Elimination

problemStatement.plain: Bridge Mathlib's `taylorWithinEval` formulation of Taylor polynomials to the explicit exponential partial sums used in the remainder estimates.
whyMatters: A clean bridge would remove an interface gap between Mathlib's general Taylor machinery and the concrete exponential-series proof.
The surrounding verified exponential estimates are useful regression tests for future axiom-elimination work.

proven: `exp_series_summable`, `exp_tsum`, and `exp_hasSum` establish the exponential power-series facts.
`exp_partial_sum_tendsto` and `exp_remainder_tendsto_zero` prove convergence of partial sums and vanishing remainders.
`iteratedDeriv_exp` records the derivative identity needed by Taylor arguments.
`exp_lagrange_remainder` proves a Lagrange-remainder bound for positive inputs.
`euler_number_series`, `euler_tsum`, and `euler_partial_sum_tendsto` specialize the series to e.
`euler_approx_error`, `exp_infinite_radius`, `exp_one_gt_two`, and `exp_five_term` provide concrete estimates and corollaries.
open: The direct equality between `taylorWithinEval` and the explicit exponential partial sum remains the named bridge target.
knownResults.goal: Close the Taylor API bridge so the exponential remainder proof can rely on Mathlib's Taylor polynomial interface without extra translation.
